toegepas.voor: Laat die bottel 'n rukkie staan, en die olie lê
toegepas.na: Laat die bottel 'n rukkie staan, dan lê die olie
toegepas.rede_vinder: An imperative followed by ', en' plus a result clause copies English 'let it stand, and the oil...'; Afrikaans links the result with 'dan' and inverts the verb.
toegepas.fout: The imperative followed by ', en' and a present-tense result clause follows the English pattern and leaves the cause-and-result link loose.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'dan lê die olie' is the natural Afrikaans way to link the action to its result, and the meaning, the order and every protected wording stay the same.

laat_vaar.voor: Om met die hand te sorteer, tel jy
laat_vaar.na: Wanneer jy met die hand sorteer, tel jy
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: An 'Om ... te'-clause opening a main clause with 'jy' mirrors English 'To sort by hand, you...'; 'Wanneer jy ...' reads more naturally at Grade 6 and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: A fronted 'Om ... te' clause is normal Afrikaans, so this is a lateral move, and it would put 'wanneer' in two sentences in a row because the next sentence starts 'Dit werk wanneer'.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: die gaatjies bly op die filter
laat_vaar_vorige.na: die gaatjies, bly op die filter
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A comma after the embedded relative clause separates its verb from the main verb 'bly' (AWS); study text only, not the protected definition.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: An optional comma, and the sentence closely repeats the decided 'filtreer' definition, which has no comma, so the two would stop matching.
